provenance.note: State machines to model explicitly in the native runtime. Transitions must be validated against oracle observations (courts) before sealing.

state_machines.name: message_pipe_endpoint
transitions: transfer -> transferred (message in flight / at remote node)
invariants: one peer identity per endpoint at a time
messages preserve ordering per public contract
closure is eventually observable
a closed endpoint cannot be resurrected
transferred handle has exactly one logical owner

state_machines.name: handle_table_entry
invariants: handle-table reuse cannot confuse stale identities (generation counters)
double close is a detectable error, never UB
close during in-flight transfer does not leak or duplicate ownership

state_machines.name: trap
transitions: arm -> armed (or fires immediately if context already satisfies)
handle close -> trigger cancelled (callback with MOJO_RESULT_CANCELLED)
invariants: a trap fires at most as permitted by its registration state
cancellation cannot produce a use-after-free callback
no callback while holding internal locks
no wakeup loss

state_machines.name: data_pipe
invariants: element-size and capacity constraints
two-phase begin/end ownership (no double begin, no end without begin)
commit sizes validated
signal transitions (READABLE/WRITABLE/PEER_CLOSED) exact

state_machines.name: shared_buffer_mapping
invariants: mapping lifetime independent of handle lifetime
read-only duplication enforced
no aliasing mutable mappings incorrectly

state_machines.name: invitation
invariants: named attachments unique
no reuse of a sent invitation
peer death before acceptance cleans up
bootstrap races handled deterministically

state_machines.name: node_routing (CoreIpcz)
invariants: ordering preserved across route changes
port transfer with queued messages
duplicate/delayed control messages tolerated
closure during migration
cleanup after node death
